interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is reported absent. Positive surgical margins is reported absent. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 48.22 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 36.17–60.28 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology is reassuring, showing a Gleason 4+5 (ISUP grade group 5) diagnosis with no extraprostatic extension, negative surgical margins, and no invasion of the seminal vesicles. Furthermore, there was no lymph node metastasis documented. These findings are favorable. Countervailing factors include the missing biopsy report for Gleason pattern and ISUP grading, which limits the full assessment of the primary tumor characteristics. Nodal status is documented as "no lymph node metastasis." The prognosis is supported by the negative margins and absence of seminal vesicle invasion. However, the postoperative PSA is not recorded, meaning biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Missing nodal sampling is not applicable as nodal status was documented. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory is crucial for revising the prognosis.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology indicates a Gleason 4+5 (ISUP grade group 5) prostate cancer with pathological stage pT2c. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins, no invasion of the seminal vesicles, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no lymph node metastasis, as documented by the surgical pathology report: "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 4+5 (ISUP grade group 5), pathological stage pT2c. There was no extraprostatic extension; surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." This is countered by the missing biopsy report regarding Gleason pattern and ISUP classification. Since nodal sampling was performed, the absence of documented nodal status is not applicable. The prognosis is supported by the negative margins and absence of nodal metastasis. However, the postoperative PSA is not recorded, meaning biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its trajectory is necessary to revise this prognosis.
